findings.title: Date overrides bypass calendar and booking conflicts
findings.description:
When an override matches the slot’s date, `checkIfIsAvailable` returns `true` before reaching `busy.every(...)`. Consequently, an ordinary event on an override day can advertise slots overlapping existing bookings, external calendar events, buffers, or booking-limit blocks returned by `getUserAvailability`.

An override should replace recurring working hours, not bypass busy-time checks. Continue through conflict validation after establishing that the slot fits the override, and add a regression test combining an override with an overlapping booking.

findings.title: Split working hours reject slots within valid intervals
findings.description:
The new check rejects a slot if **any** working-hours interval on that weekday does not contain it. For a schedule with 09:00–12:00 and 13:00–17:00 intervals, a valid 09:00 slot passes the first interval but is rejected against the afternoon interval. Afternoon slots are similarly rejected against the morning interval, potentially removing the entire day’s availability.

Instead, require at least one matching interval to contain the complete slot. The `end` calculation also currently uses `slotStartTime`; containment must account for `slotEndTime`. Cover split schedules and slots extending beyond an interval’s end.

findings.title: Multiple override intervals invalidate one another
findings.description:
The override search returns an unavailable result as soon as it finds a same-day interval entirely before or after the slot, even if another interval contains that slot. With overrides of 09:00–12:00 and 13:00–17:00, a 09:00–10:00 slot is rejected against the afternoon override, while a 13:00–14:00 slot is rejected against the morning override.

Collect the applicable override intervals and accept schedule containment when **any one** contains the full slot, then apply busy-time checks. Add a test with two override intervals on the same date and verify availability in both intervals and unavailability in the gap.
